purpose: Test whether wood bearing must govern simply because its Mode Im reference is below isolated A307 shaft shear. It need not: bending-dominated Mode IV can be lower in a defined but different wood-to-steel assembly.
assumptions: one 3/8-inch full-body bolt, one shear plane, sound 1.5-inch solid Douglas Fir-Larch wood main member
hypothetical 1/4-inch ASTM A36 steel side plate; this is not the 12-gauge formed A66
full-body shank at wood and steel bearing zones, no gap, prying or bolt-axis tension
dry NDS reference conditions with no geometry, service, group, or duration adjustments
steel bearing 87,000 psi and bolt bending yield 45,000 psi are supplied reference assumptions, not delivered-product certificates
interpretation: For this assumed A36-plate assembly, NDS Mode IV is below Mode Im in both grain directions. This refutes a universal first-failure claim based only on wood bearing versus bolt shaft shear. The actual A66 has different, unverified steel thickness/bearing and geometry, so no A66 failure order or capacity follows.
